entry_mapping_check: each handler entry loads its own NULL fault template, 0x781e80 + 0x14*i in source order
method: black-box sequences of 1-3 random ops over 9 entry points; nanopb stream/ostream/decode/encode stubbed (decode/encode return 1/0/0x100/0x201/0x301, random errmsg, bytes_written incl. >0xffff), health data manager save stubs (uint8 results 0/1/0xff/random byte), BLE tx, fault handler; command ids 0-5 and random, NULL frame/args, highlight counts 0-3; float logs walked as doubles; 600 tests + 60 per mutant (bias toward mutated entry)
observed: all callee args and return values, logs incl. %f args, fault records, encoded message hash; rx message (0x31c), tx message (0x31c) and tx packet (0x100) after every op
test_notes: first run 482/600: all diffs came from save stubs returning values >0xff from functions declared uint8_t. clang trusts the AAPCS callee extension of a uint8 result, stock IAR re-narrows; real callees are C uint8_t functions, so stubs now return uint8-range values
